baseline.sourceIdentityVerification: Every tracked file in the archived capture checkout matched its baseline Git blob; current HEAD:src also matched at checkpoint time.

capture.imageExclusions: No exclusion rectangle appeared in the baseline first viewports; the canonical future map-tile and user-image exclusion rule remains active.
capture.runtime: Clean git archive of the baseline commit, Next.js production build on loopback, and deterministic out-of-tree Supabase Auth/PostgREST fixture.
capture.artifactDrift: REPINNED 2026-09-14, and the drift is worth recording rather than quietly fixing. Three pinned harnesses had changed without their hashes moving with them: reproduce.sh, when its macOS-only default working directory and browser path were parameterised so it runs on Linux; capture.mjs, when `ready` and `measure` moved out to measure.mjs so both halves of the relative comparison read the page with one copy of the code; and verify.mjs itself, in this change. The pin worked the first time anyone ran the verifier - it failed on capture.mjs immediately - and that is the finding: NOTHING RUNS THE VERIFIER. It is not a pnpm script and not a CI job, so a hash pin that is only checked by hand catches drift whenever someone happens to look, which here was three commits late. `pnpm density:verify` exists now so it at least has a name. Wiring it into CI needs one thing this change does not have: the job checks out at depth 1 and the verifier reads the frozen baseline commit through `git archive`, so it would need the history fetched before it could run at all.

pixelCoverage.rule: Exclude every pixel whose centre lies inside a marked element from both the ink numerator and the included-pixel denominator.

decoratedElementBudget.rule: Exclude only a visible direct text node beneath the required-accuracy marker from the budgeted text contribution. Never exclude its pixels, descendants for another reason, border, filled background, or background image. Raw decorated counts are never reduced.

interactiveBudget.rule: The exclusions apply only to interactiveElementCount; rawInteractiveElementCount and focusableElementCount remain diagnostic and unmodified.

methodology.ink: Convert screenshot sRGB to CIELAB with the D65/2 degree reference white and count an included pixel as ink when CIEDE2000 deltaE00 against #f7f8f1 is at least 8.
methodology.whiteSpace: 1 - inkCoverageRatio on exactly the same included-pixel denominator.
methodology.exactGroundRatio: Diagnostic only: exact sRGB equality with #f7f8f1 among included pixels.
methodology.screenshotHash: SHA-256 of the exact encoded PNG bytes.
methodology.pixelExclusions: At DPR 1, exclude a pixel when its centre is inside a rectangle emitted by the canonical pixel-exclusion selector; overlapping rectangles exclude a pixel once.
methodology.interactive: First-viewport interactive elements, with the interactive-only exclusions declared above.
methodology.visibleText: Normalized direct text-node characters whose rendered range intersects the first viewport; navigation remains included.
methodology.decoratedElements: Raw counts include every first-viewport element carrying visible direct text, a nonzero border, a filled background, or a background image. Budgeted counts apply only the required-accuracy direct-text exclusion declared above; visual decoration still counts.
methodology.primaryContentPadding: Use the content edge (left border edge plus computed padding-left) of the canonical primary-content marker when present. Otherwise use the minimum left edge of visible direct-text ranges and visible controls/media inside main or role=main, falling back to body, while excluding navigation, footer, Copilot, and aria-hidden content.
methodology.proseMeasure: For every rendered p and li, divide its rendered width by the measured advance of ten zero glyphs using that element’s computed font properties.
methodology.adjacentSections: Use canonical top-level-section markers when present; otherwise use unnested semantic section elements inside primary content. The gap is next.top minus previous.bottom in DOM order.
methodology.primaryClaim: Within the canonical primary-claim marker, count visible elements carrying direct text and visible figure, svg, canvas, data-figure-kind, or role=img descendants.
methodology.horizontalOverflow: documentElement.scrollWidth minus viewport width; at 390px the maximum is zero.
methodology.canonicalManifestHash: Sort matching files by repository-relative POSIX path. For each raw file, append `<sha256>  <path>\n` with two ASCII spaces. SHA-256 the concatenated UTF-8 lines; absolute paths and enumeration order are excluded.

relativeComparison.rule: For each successorRouteId above, post-change ink coverage must be no more than 60% of the mapped baseline route's ink coverage at the same viewport and state. This is brief X6.2 verbatim - "where a route has a baseline predecessor, its ink coverage is <= 60% of that predecessor's" - and the threshold is thresholds.whiteSpace.successorInkCoverageMaxFractionOfPredecessor, 0.6.
relativeComparison.unmappedNewRoutes: absolute budgets apply; relative comparison is not applicable because no honest baseline predecessor exists
relativeComparison.derivation: Not authored here. Every row is read out of docs/route-register.json: a baseline route the register still carries with a redirect disposition maps to that disposition's target, and one the register keeps maps to itself. scripts/density-successors.test.ts rebuilds this list from the register and compares it, so a rename that moves a successor fails rather than leaving a comparison pointing at the wrong page. Derived 2026-09-11; all 22 baseline routes resolve, so `unmappedNewRoutes` describes no route today.
relativeComparison.proposedChange: PROPOSED AND DECLINED, 2026-09-14. The 60% stands. Asked whether a successor should be held to 60% of its predecessor's ink or merely to no more than 100%, the operator first chose no-denser. The question had not put X6.2's own clause in front of them: the brief states the 60%, gives its reason in its summary line - "the brief asks for far more white space than today, so an absolute floor alone would let today's app pass unchanged" - and closes with "ceilings may be lowered, never raised", which makes 0.6 to 1.0 the one direction that needs a signature rather than an engineer's judgement. Asked again with all three facts, the operator KEPT THE BRIEF'S NUMBER. So the threshold here is 0.6, item 14 of docs/protocol/brief-corrections-proposed.md is marked declined and kept whole, and the measured consequence stands as the record: 3 of 44 at 0.6 against 26 of 44 at 1.0. The evidence still scores every row against both, because a verdict that cannot be re-read under the other rule is a number nobody can check.

postChange.reason: Still pending, and the blocker is now MEASURED rather than asserted. Three facts stand from 2026-09-11: the successor map carries all 22 rows so the relative rule has something to compare against; the 44px control scale landed on 2026-09-11 and changes the rendered height of every surface carrying a link, so this capture is owed rather than optional; and ink coverage is a pixel measurement taken on macOS 26.5.1 arm64 with Google Chrome 151. MEASURED 2026-09-14. scripts/density-baseline/reproduce.sh was run on Linux (6.18.44 x86_64, Chromium 141.0.7390.37, Node 22.22.2) against the same frozen baseline commit, and the two captures were compared route by route. Ink coverage is systematically HIGHER on Linux: mean +28.5% relative at 390x844 (max +41.4%) and +26.5% at 1280x800 (max +36.6%), on identical markup. Against a relative rule whose threshold is 60% of the baseline, a platform shift of that size is not noise, so the equivalence requirement is confirmed with evidence rather than by argument. AND THE BLOCKER IS NARROWER THAN IT LOOKED. Every non-pixel measure was IDENTICAL across the two platforms: interactive element counts, visible text character counts and prose element counts matched on all 44 captures, zero differences. So only inkCoverageRatio, whiteSpaceRatio and exactGroundRatio need one machine; the element and text budgets never did. THE SECOND BLOCKER, WHICH WAS NOT RECORDED BEFORE AND IS THE LARGER ONE: there is no post-change capture harness. capture.mjs reads contract.routes, which are the BASELINE's 22 paths, and the post-change side must measure their successors - six of which are authenticated and three of which carry a dynamic segment (/genome/[subject]/ancestry, /genome/[subject]/data/browser, /genome/[subject]/reports, /copilot/[scope]) that needs a concrete value. supabase-fixture.mjs cannot serve them: it is built FROM the baseline checkout (it reads that tree's data/templates, providers and sample genome) and stubs that product's PostgREST tables, while HEAD's authenticated pages read a much larger surface through the service role. Completing this needs either a HEAD-shaped fixture or the real local stack the browser suite already builds, plus a successor route list with concrete parameters. That is the work; the platform equivalence is a constraint on where it runs, not the reason it has not been done. PROGRESS 2026-09-14, and the recorded blocker is now half closed. (1) THE MEASUREMENT CODE IS ONE COPY. `ready` and `measure` moved to scripts/density-baseline/measure.mjs and capture.mjs imports them, because a second driver with a second copy of the reading code would have made the two halves of this comparison incomparable by drift - the exact failure this document exists to prevent. Proven unchanged rather than assumed: the frozen baseline was re-captured on Linux with the extracted module and compared against the pre-extraction Linux capture of the same morning - 0 measurement differences across all 44 captures and all 44 screenshots byte-identical. (2) THE SUCCESSOR URLS ARE DECLARED. postChange.measurementPaths carries one row per baseline route with the concrete URL to capture, the surface that decides whether the capture signs in, and the parameters behind every dynamic segment. Five successors carry one - four take the account's own `me` subject segment, and the report takes the baseline's OWN slug (type-2-diabetes-tcf7l2-rs7903146, still published) so the comparison is one page against the page that replaced it rather than against a different report that happens to render. scripts/density-successors.test.ts checks all of it against the register and the baseline. WHAT REMAINS is the driver and the run: a capture that signs into a HEAD build on the real local stack, plus a synthetic source covering both the AIM panel and chr10:112998590 so the ancestry map and that one report are in the same state their predecessors were measured in. Both halves must also use one browser build, which the Linux baseline now fixes at the Playwright Chromium the e2e suite already installs. CAPTURED AND COMPARED 2026-09-14, AND THE RELATIVE RULE IS NOT MET ANYWHERE IT CAN HONESTLY BE APPLIED. Both halves were measured on one Linux machine with one browser build, 22 routes and 44 measurements on each side, and the row-by-row result is in postChange.comparison with its evidence under docs/evidence/density-post-change/. Against brief X6.2 - a successor's ink coverage at or below 60% of its predecessor's - three of the 44 pass and 41 do not, median ratio 0.9369. All three passes are on routes whose baseline predecessor was partly a fixture author's choice of numbers rather than a computed result, so among the 28 measurements with an honest predecessor there are none. The status is measured-with-findings rather than measured for that reason and for one more: 16 rows have no honest predecessor at all, which is recorded in comparison.noHonestPredecessor and which the absolute budgets answer instead - see comparison.absoluteBudgets, where the rewrite misses 84 against the baseline's 103, with 20 fixed - eight of them in this change, every authenticated mobile surface's primary-content left padding - and exactly one new. Neither the recorded baseline numbers nor the 44 evidence screenshots were swapped; see comparison.notSwapped.

comparison.rule: ratio = post-change inkCoverageRatio / baseline inkCoverageRatio, at the same baseline route and the same viewport. withinBriefRule is ratio <= 0.6, which is brief X6.2's relative rule and the threshold docs/density-baseline.json carries. withinProposedRule is ratio <= 1.0, the operator's stated preference, which is not in force: X6.2 says ceilings may be lowered, never raised, so it needs a signed brief correction first.
comparison.platform: Both halves on one machine: Linux 6.18.44 x86_64, Chromium 141.0.7390.37, Node 22.22.2, light theme, DPR 1, locale en-US, timezone UTC, service workers blocked. That is the requirement this document recorded on 2026-09-11 and it is met rather than waived: re-running the frozen baseline on Linux instead of macOS moves ink coverage by a mean of +28.5% at 390x844 and +26.5% at 1280x800 on identical markup, which is larger than most of the differences being looked for.

The tree measured was f86e2f428b3b7b38dd867aedd9874e408c6c63b3, which is byte-identical to the tree of 445664bfbaafaa81327082be84e8b2ac5764304f. The computed file's own baseline.commitSha field is a header inherited from this contract and does not describe that half.

named.finding: THE HEADLINE: no measurement with an honest predecessor meets the rule. Zero of 28.
named.rows: All 44. Within X6.2 (<= 0.6): 3. Over: 41. Median 0.9369, range 0.3663 to 1.5002.
named.evidence: All three measurements that meet the rule are on the two routes whose baseline predecessor was partly a fixture author's choice of numbers rather than a computed result - /genome/me/ancestry at 1280x800 (0.5375) and /genome/me/reports at both viewports (0.5126 and 0.3663). See noHonestPredecessor below. Strip those out and the 28 measurements whose predecessors were real pages showing real content contain no passes at all: the public twenty run 0.6411 to 1.1366 (median 0.8471) and the auth eight 1.1001 to 1.1482.
named.reading: X6.2 does not ask the successors to be no denser. It asks them to be 40% sparser, and says why: "the brief asks for far more white space than today, so an absolute floor alone would let today's app pass unchanged". Measured, today's app does pass the absolute floor - all 44 measurements clear the 0.62 white-space minimum on both halves, see absoluteBudgets - and fails the relative rule everywhere it can honestly be applied. The brief's own justification for having a relative rule at all is confirmed by the first measurement ever taken against it.

named.finding: The public surfaces did not get sparser; three of them got denser, and these rows carry nothing to argue about.
named.rows: Twenty measurements, median 0.8471, range 0.6411 to 1.1366, none within 0.6. Above 1.0: /changelog 1.1366 and 1.0996, / 1.0782 and 1.0673, /providers 1.0711.
named.evidence: No file feeds these pages, no accessibility rule explains them, and their predecessors were ordinary rendered pages. Interactive counts are flat (6 and 6, 6 and 6, 4 and 4; /changelog at 390x844 went 6 to 5). What moved is text: /changelog 949 to 1,022 characters at 1280x800 and 557 to 680 at 390x844, the home page 522 to 541 and 581 to 600, /providers 783 to 897.
named.reading: The cleanest reading available of what the rewrite did to density: essentially nothing, with three surfaces drifting denser as sentences were added over five months. Twenty of twenty outside the rule. This is where the work starts if the 60% is to be met, because it is the only block of rows where neither the measurement nor the predecessor is arguable.

named.finding: The four auth surfaces are the clearest rise in the comparison, and the cause is the 44px control scale.
named.rows: /auth/sign-in, /auth/sign-up, /auth/forgot-password, /auth/reset-password at both viewports; ratios 1.1001 to 1.1482, median 1.1299.
named.evidence: These rows control themselves. Visible text character counts are IDENTICAL across the two halves on three of the four pages (141 and 141, 161 and 161, 192 and 192) and differ by two characters on the fourth (358 and 356). The same words, in the same layout, rendering 10% to 15% more ink. The 44px control scale landed on 2026-09-11 and is the only change that touches these pages; an auth page is a heading, a sentence and two or three controls, so raising every control to 44px raises its ink share by roughly this much by construction.
named.reading: Not a defect. ADR-0029 already decided this collision in terms: when the accessibility rule and the density budget conflict, the accessibility rule wins and the baseline is re-captured. A target a person cannot hit is a surface they cannot use; a density overrun is a surface that is harder to read. These eight rows are that decision showing up in the numbers, and the answer it prescribes is re-capture, not redesign.

named.finding: /overview at 390x844 was the largest rise at 1.8039. It is 1.5002 now, and the change is in the product rather than in the measurement.
named.evidence: The predecessor showed four number cards above the fold - reports covered 151/151, polygenic scores 3, mtDNA haplogroup H, files 1 - each a label, a large numeral and one line. The successor showed the plain-language distinction between a statistical estimate and a specific-variant report, two headed paragraphs of it, over a persistent bottom navigation bar the predecessor did not have. The operator called the mobile figure a defect and the desktop one not, and the fix is the pattern /genome/[subject]/reports already uses for these same two sentences: the count and its short gloss stay visible, the full definition is one keyboard-operable disclosure away. 245 of 574 visible characters left the first viewport; ink fell 17%. The character count went UP to 639, because the freed height pulled two more domain cards above the fold - which is why the ink measurement and the text measurement disagree here and the ink one is the answer.
named.reading: Still 1.50, and the remainder is structural: three domain cards with descriptions plus the bottom navigation bar, against a predecessor with four numerals and no bar. Getting below 1.0 means removing content or navigation, which is a product decision rather than a density fix, so it stops here and the number is recorded as it stands.

named.finding: /settings at 1280x800 is now the largest rise: 1.4208, and it is the only NEW absolute-budget miss in the rewrite.
named.rows: inkCoverageRatio 0.033942 -> 0.048226; visible text 612 -> 996 characters, against a 700 cap.
named.evidence: The sex-chromosome section landed on 2026-09-14 and sits in the first viewport at this width: three short paragraphs saying what the record is used for, that Inherit does not work it out from the file, and what a family member can see if it is recorded, followed by the options. That is the 384 extra characters almost exactly, and it is the single row in absoluteBudgets marked new-in-the-rewrite.
named.reading: The operator decided this one is not a defect: the prose is the reason the section is allowed to exist at all - a declared record with a narrow stated use and a visible consequence - and removing the explanation to save ink would remove the part that makes it honest. Recorded as an accepted breach of the 700-character budget rather than quietly dropped, because it is the only budget this rewrite newly broke. The same route at 390x844 is 0.8699: at mobile width the section falls below the fold.

named.finding: The largest fall is /reports -> /genome/me/reports at 1280x800: 0.3657, with MORE text, not less - and it is one of only three rows that meet the brief, all of which have no honest predecessor.

noHonestPredecessor.status: MEASURED 2026-09-14. This replaces the fixture confound recorded earlier, which understated it.
noHonestPredecessor.what: The earlier record said the two halves were fed different synthetic sources and that closing the gap meant driving one file through both. Reading scripts/density-baseline/supabase-fixture.mjs settles it differently and more sharply: THE BASELINE HALF DOES NOT READ A FILE FOR ITS DERIVED RESULTS. It is a PostgREST stub, and three of the four derived layers the authenticated pages show are literals in that file - the admixture result (EUR 0.54, AFR 0.18, EAS 0.12, SAS 0.10, AMR 0.06, markersUsed 82, "82 of 120 ancestry markers covered in this synthetic fixture"), the mtDNA call (haplogroup H, matched 5 of 7) and the Y call (not determined), and the three polygenic scores (percentiles 62, 33 and 78; coverages 0.82, 0.74 and 0.69). Only variant_calls came from the sample, and it came in at GRCh37 positions the baseline app read directly.
noHonestPredecessor.consequence: No choice of upload on the HEAD side can reproduce a number that was never computed, so those measurements have no honest predecessor and X6.2's own answer applies - the one this document already carries in relativeComparison.unmappedNewRoutes: the absolute budgets stand and the relative comparison is not applicable, because inventing a predecessor produces a number that means nothing. /genome/me/ancestry is the clearest case and the panel sizes say why on their own: the baseline's page names 120 ancestry markers, the shipped estimator reads 168.
noHonestPredecessor.scope: Wholly invented: /ancestry, 2 measurements. Partly: /reports, whose predecessor's first viewport was three polygenic cards with invented percentiles and filled progress bars, and /dashboard, whose predecessor showed the invented haplogroup as one of four cards - 4 measurements. Genuinely file-driven on both sides and therefore closable by matching the source: /browse and /reports/[slug], 4 measurements. Not result-driven at all and unaffected: /chat, /settings, /uploads, 6 measurements. And the 28 public and auth measurements were never in question.
noHonestPredecessor.whyItWasNotClosed: The operator asked for one file through both halves. It cannot be done for the six invented measurements at all, and for the four file-driven ones it needs the baseline's own 2,135-variant sample uploaded to HEAD - which covers 5 of the 168 shipped ancestry markers, three percent, far below the reliability floor, so it would take /genome/me/ancestry off its map and trade one incomparable row for another. The measurement that settles this is in the numbers already: strike all 16 authenticated rows and the verdict does not move, because 0 of the remaining 28 meet the rule either. Spending a capture run to make six rows comparable would not change a single conclusion in this document.

absoluteBudgets.what: Every absolute threshold in this document, applied to all 44 measurements of BOTH halves, with each miss labelled pre-existing, new or fixed. Recorded because the relative rule is not applicable on 16 rows and the absolute budgets are what X6.2 says applies instead.
absoluteBudgets.reading:
THE WHITE-SPACE FLOOR CATCHES NOTHING: all 44 measurements clear 0.62 on both halves, by a wide margin - post-change ink runs 0.0265 to 0.1353, so white space runs 0.865 to 0.973. That is the brief's own argument for the relative rule, measured. THE REWRITE DID NOT DEGRADE THE ABSOLUTE BUDGETS AND HAS NOW IMPROVED THEM: 103 misses on the baseline against 84 on the successors, 83 of them the same miss on both sides, 20 fixed and exactly ONE new - /settings' 996 characters against the 700 cap, which the operator has accepted. Eight of the twenty were fixed in this change: every authenticated mobile surface rendered 16px of primary-content left padding against a 24px minimum, because the app shell's
carried px-4 below md. It carries px-6 from 360px up and all eight read 24. The breakpoint is not decoration - raising the gutter at every width narrowed /genome/[subject]/data/browser by 16px and pushed igv.js's own overflow from the 446 CSS px recorded in docs/accessibility-divergence.json to 454, failing the 320px reflow check. This document's rule is measured at 390px and that one at 320px, so stepping the gutter at 360px satisfies both rather than trading one for the other (D-119). AND THE ESTIMATE OF HOW MANY WERE THE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN THE PRODUCT WAS MINE, WAS PUBLISHED AS A READING, AND TOOK TWO MEASUREMENTS TO GET RIGHT. First it was "roughly 57 of the 83", a guess. Then, having measured only the prose ELEMENT TYPE, it was "about six" - also wrong, because the second thing the measure gets wrong had not been tested yet. Both are now measured and recorded in docs/evidence/density-post-change/absolute-budgets.json#briefsOwnProseBasis. (1) THE ELEMENT TYPE: the contract reads every rendered `p` OR `li` anywhere in the document; the brief says "prose

" and explains the 45ch floor by arithmetic on the content column. On the brief's wording the floor is missed on 15 of 22 routes rather than 21, with 2 more carrying no paragraph in primary content at all - six rows change verdict. (2) THE BOX VERSUS THE LINE: both of those read the element's BOX, and a block paragraph fills its column, so a short sentence in a wide container reports a wide measure while rendering no long line. Measuring the longest line a paragraph actually renders, /files reports a 112ch box against a 56ch line and / reports 112ch against 59ch - two more rows that are the measurement. THAT DISTINCTION ALSO FOUND SEVEN REAL DEFECTS THE BOX BASIS COULD NOT SEPARATE OUT: the legal and about surfaces genuinely rendered 85ch LINES, and src/components/legal/legal-page.tsx now caps its prose, taking them to 63-65ch. So the honest count is eight of the 83 are the measurement, seven were real and are fixed here, and the rest are the product. Filed as D-115. The section-gap measure is wrong in MAGNITUDE rather than verdict: it reads `next.top - previous.bottom`, the space BETWEEN boxes, while the legal layout separates sections with `border-t` plus `py-8` INSIDE each, so /about reports 0 where a reader sees 64px - still short of 96, so those misses stand. WHAT IS LEFT IS 27 ROWS: 21 measurements exceed the 700-character visible-text cap, which is a copy decision on every surface; /auth/sign-in and /auth/sign-up carry 9 and 10 first-viewport interactive elements against 7, where the count includes the wordmark link and the footer's "Back to Inherit" - wrapping those in a navigation landmark, the pattern src/components/site/app-shell.tsx already uses, would take sign-in to 7, and whether that is honest marking or shaping the measurement is an owner's call rather than mine; and /genome/me/ancestry and /genome/me/reports carry 48 and 42 decorated elements at 390x844 against 40, which means removing visual chrome. None of those three is an engineering fix.
